chunks: Muhammad b. Yahya, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa, from Hammad b. Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad b. Muslim and Buray al-Ijali who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to Humran b. A'yan regarding something he had asked him: 'Indeed, the people are destroyed because they do not ask.'

key_terms.إِنَّمَا: a particle of exclusivity/restriction, meaning 'none other than' or 'the only reason is'
key_terms.يَسْأَلُونَ: ask/inquire — seeking knowledge from qualified scholars
key_terms.يَهْلِكُ: perish/are destroyed — used for both spiritual and worldly ruin

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq say people perish because they do not ask?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delivers a striking observation to Humran b. A'yan — one of the trusted inner circle of companions — during a private teaching moment. The Imam declares that the root cause of human destruction and loss is the failure to ask questions of those who possess knowledge. This hadith appears in the chapter on seeking knowledge from scholars, underscoring that religious ignorance, when left unaddressed through inquiry, leads to spiritual and moral ruin.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim and Bureyd Al Ijaly who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Humran Bin Ayn regarding something he had asked him<sup>asws</sup>: ‘But rather, the people are destroyed because they are not asking’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Hammed ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurra, Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd al-‘Ijli who has said the following.
“(Imam) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘People are destroyed only because they do not ask (what they do not know).’”
